related_questions.question: How effective is Paxlovid against COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: Paxlovid is generally considered effective in reducing the risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes. Studies have shown it can significantly reduce the risk of hospitalization and death, particularly when taken early in the course of infection. Specifically, one study showed an 86% reduction in hospitalization or death from any cause when Paxlovid was taken within five days of symptom onset, according to Yale Medicine. However, it is not effective in relieving symptoms of Long COVID.
snippet_highlighted_words: generally considered effective in reducing the risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes

list.title: Effectiveness against severe illness:
list.snippet: Paxlovid is primarily designed to prevent severe illness in individuals at higher risk of complications from COVID-19. Studies have demonstrated its ability to reduce the likelihood of hospitalization and death.

list.title: Early treatment is key:
list.snippet: The effectiveness of Paxlovid is greatest when started within five days of symptom onset. This timing allows the medication to interfere with the virus replication process early in the infection.

list.title: No impact on Long COVID:
list.snippet: A recent study indicated that Paxlovid does not alleviate symptoms associated with Long COVID.

related_questions.question: Is Paxlovid a COVID-19 antibody treatment?
related_questions.snippet: UPMC does not offer monoclonal antibodies for COVID-19. It has been shown to not be effective with the variants that are currently in our community. If you have COVID-19, as an alternative you may also be eligible for Paxlovid, an antiviral medicine taken by mouth, available at retail pharmacies with a prescription.

related_questions.question: Does Paxlovid stop COVID from being contagious?
related_questions.snippet: You can still spread the virus while taking Paxlovid, and how long you are contagious depends on many factors. In addition to possibly making you less contagious, Paxlovid has been shown to lower the risk of hospitalization from COVID-19 infection by over 50% and the risk of death by 75%.
